text:
Sophie L.: 🔔 Customer acme-inc hitting intermittent JSON decode failures in JSON mode (streaming). They only see it on long responses with streaming enabled. Error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter. Repro attached below.

Emma C.: ugh, customer impact. Can you paste a minimal repro and the raw stream chunks?

Sophie L.: repro steps: 1) python SDK v1.4.2, response_mode='json' and stream=True 2) send a long structured response with array of items 3) sometimes the streamed payload that hits the client is missing a comma between array elements when a server heartbeat chunk is emitted.

Sophie L.: raw stream example (from tcpdump):
```
data: {"items":[{"id":1,"name":"a"}]}

data: {"heartbeat":true}

data: {"items":[{"id":2,"name":"b"}],"meta":{"cursor":42}}

data: [DONE]
```

Sophie L.: When client concatenates chunks naively you get: `{"items":[{"id":1,"name":"a"}]}{"heartbeat":true}{"items":[{"id":2,"name":"b"}],"meta":{"cursor":42}}` which obviously is invalid JSON. Customer schema validator fails during ingest.

Raj P.: thanks. Sounds like our python streaming iterator is yielding raw event payloads without inserting separators between top-level JSON objects. Historically we relied on ndjson but json-mode was added and we didn't add a joiner. Might be a regression from streaming refactor.

Oliver M.: tagging support-bot for associated incident link: <https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-1023|INC-2026-1023> :eyes:

SupportBot: Incident INC-2026-1023 created (priority P2) — assigned to eng-ml.

Emma C.: quick mitigation for customer: 1) set stream=False (non-streaming) OR 2) switch to ndjson mode if they can parse ndjson OR 3) temporary server-side change to avoid sending heartbeat events for json-mode. Which is least disruptive?

Sophie L.: customer tried stream=False but saw latency spikes; ndjson is heavier lift for them. They asked if SDK can auto-handle heartbeats.

Raj P.: short-term PR: python SDK should treat json-mode streaming as a sequence of complete JSON chunks separated by the server's event boundaries. When concatenating, if two top-level objects are adjacent we should emit a comma into the reconstructed buffer when we're inside an array context. But we need to detect context — risky. Safer is to wrap each chunk in an outer envelope then merge on the client. I'll open a repro branch.

Oliver M.: can you dump the exact exception and stacktrace customer got? Sophie?

Sophie L.: stacktrace (client):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 128, in <module>
    payload = json.loads(full_streamed_string)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/json/__init__.py", line 346, in loads
    return _default_decoder.decode(s)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/json/decoder.py", line 337, in decode
    obj, end = self.raw_decode(s, idx=_w(s, 0).end())
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 40 (char 39)
```

Sophie L.: customer also included SDK logs showing our iterator yielding three data chunks with no separators.

Emma C.: escalation notes: affecting one major customer pipeline; they've paused ingestion -> revenue impact. Need fast follow.

Raj P.: Plan: (A) hotfix patch in python-sdk to detect adjacent top-level JSON objects and insert comma when reconstructing stream inside an array OR (B) fallback: treat json-mode streaming as sequence of independent JSON documents and emit them separately to caller (change API shape). I'll prototype A and test with their capture.

Oliver M.: can you also reproduce in ts-sdk? Might be a shared server behavior but different SDK parsers handle it differently.

Raj P.: good point. I ran a quick node repro and the ts client merges chunks into a buffer similarly and fails too. So server is emitting heartbeat as separate JSON object between array items. We should either change server to emit heartbeats as comments or as separate event metadata outside the JSON body. I'll file a runtime change as well.

Sophie L.: customer ok with temporary disable of heartbeats if we can promise a patch timeline. ETA?

Raj P.: patch branch open: github.com/redwood/sdk-python/pulls/432 — initial fix adds a joiner when we detect we're inside an array. Test coverage added. If tests pass, aim for canary release today and stable tomorrow.

Emma C.: copy that. I'll update customer and schedule a customer call for tomorrow morning. Add notes to the incident. :thumbsup:

Oliver M.: leaving a note — long-term we should standardize streaming JSON envelope (server -> event-stream with type=event, data contains ndjson or framed chunks) so clients don't need heuristics. Logged: https://redwood.product/feature/FR-2312

Sophie L.: thanks team — I'll post follow-ups in this thread after customer call. :pray:
